extracted.intended_audience: agencies submitting Federal Register documents, attorneys/drafters of Federal Register text, researchers and members of the public using FederalRegister.gov and participating in rulemaking
extracted.subtask_short: using FederalRegister.gov and drafting FR documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, searching, citing, and interacting with Federal Register documents on FederalRegister.gov, and for members of the public who wish to view or comment on those documents. Covers legal status, drafting resources, accessibility, commenting procedures, and developer/API use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal status of FederalRegister.gov content
rubrics_metrics.description: This site displays a prototype of a 'Web 2.0' version of the daily Federal Register. It is not an official legal edition and does not replace the official print version or the official electronic version on GPO's govinfo.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The documents posted are XML renditions and each includes a link to the corresponding official PDF on govinfo.gov. Users relying on FederalRegister.gov for legal research should verify results against an official edition. Until the Administrative Committee of the Federal Register (ACFR) grants official status, the XML rendition on FederalRegister.gov does not provide legal notice to the public or judicial notice to the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Inspection preview guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Public Inspection web page offers a preview of documents scheduled to appear in the next day's Federal Register issue and may include documents scheduled for later issues at the agency's request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Public Inspection page to access important or complex documents before they publish in the official edition; it provides early public access but does not change legal publication status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission channels and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov's 'Site Feedback' tool and Federal Register email addresses are only intended for technical questions and comments on website functionality and cannot be used to submit comments on agency rulemaking actions or petitions on public policy issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site has no authority or ability to process rulemaking comments. Use Regulations.gov (the official docket system) or the integrated 'Submit a Formal Comment' feature (which works with Regulations.gov) to submit comments on rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special filing procedure during government shutdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: During an appropriations lapse, agencies without appropriations that wish to submit a document to the Office of the Federal Register (OFR) must attach a special handling letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If data feeds are not available from GPO during a shutdown and FederalRegister.gov is not updated, use the official edition of the Federal Register on Govinfo. The OFR may not offer technical support for FederalRegister.gov during a lapse; follow OFR Notices (e.g., 83 FR 63540) for instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active links in document text
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency has included links as part of the document text, FederalRegister.gov activates those links using the text in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links may not work if the link in the published document contained an error or if the target website is no longer at that location. Agencies should ensure included links are correct; the site also provides automated legal links where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document utility bar and sidebar features
rubrics_metrics.description: A document utility bar runs along the left side of the document and scrolls with the user; it provides access to the Public Inspection version, the official electronic format (e.g., govinfo PDF), printing, and sharing functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users can access Public Inspection and official electronic formats via the utility bar icons; use these features to get official PDFs or to share/print documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document drafting resources and handbooks
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov links to drafting and research resources such as the Drafting Document Drafting Handbook, Incorporation by Reference (IBR) Handbook, Federal Register Bulletins, and other tools to help draft Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafters should consult these handbooks for procedural and formatting requirements when preparing submissions for publication in the Federal Register (e.g., how to handle incorporation by reference, required formats, and Office of the Federal Register procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language and Plain Writing Act guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance and resources are provided for implementing the Plain Writing Act of 2010 and using plain-language drafting tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the Final Guidance on Implementing the Plain Writing Act, use PlainLanguage.gov tools, and other plain-language resources to improve clarity and accessibility of Federal Register documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference (IBR) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The site refers drafters to an IBR Handbook to understand requirements for incorporation by reference in Federal Register documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the IBR Handbook procedures to ensure that materials incorporated by reference meet legal and procedural standards (e.g., availability, citation format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search and citation best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov supports basic and advanced search tools; documents can be searched by citation (e.g., '75 FR 12345').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the advanced search for more precise queries and the citation format when searching for or referencing specific Federal Register entries; the site provides examples and search strategies for both basic and complex searches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linking and citation patterns to FederalRegister.gov
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents on FederalRegister.gov can be linked in several ways depending on the document and preferred pattern; Federal Register documents can be cited in a variety of ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the 'Linking to FederalRegister.gov' guidance for examples and recommended patterns for linking and citing Federal Register documents in external publications or online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Developer and API use standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register data originates from files used to produce print/PDF editions and is transformed into bulk XML and MODS metadata files; the site provides a REST API and documentation, plus API client libraries (e.g., a Ruby gem).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Developers and data users should use the REST API and API clients for programmatic access; review interactive documentation, GitHub repositories, and MODS metadata guidance to properly ingest and use Federal Register data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source code and reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is a fully open source project with source code available on GitHub in repositories (e.g., federalregister-api-core).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users and developers may examine, reuse, or contribute to the source code. The repositories contain code for importing Federal Register data and serving API responses; note active cleanup and maintenance notes in repos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: FederalRegister.gov is designed following Section 508 and W3C accessibility design guidelines and uses text-based files and Adobe PDF files which are text-accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents are intended to be accessible through Adobe PDF Tools and other assistive technologies; contact information is provided for access assistance for visually impaired users and for other accessibility concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA applicability to Federal Register publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal Register publications, including the FederalRegister.gov website and its various editions, are not subject to the request-for-records provisions of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under FOIA, these publications are treated differently from other agency records; consult the FOIA guidance on the site for details about what is and is not subject to FOIA.
